questions.stem: The aqueous outflow system includes various structures such as trabecular meshwork, Schlemm’s canal and collector channels. Which of the following statements is correct about this system?

options.label: A
options.text: Trabecular meshwork consists of four layers.

options.label: B
options.text: Corneoscleral meshwork forms the outermost portion of trabecular meshwork,

options.label: C
options.text: Uveal meshwork mainly offers normal resistance to the aqueous outflow.

options.label: D
options.text: Uveal meshwork extends from the iris root and ciliary body to the Schwalbe’s line.

questions.answerText: Uveal meshwork extends from the iris root and ciliary body to the Schwalbe’s line.
questions.solutionHtml:
Uveal meshwork extends from the iris root and ciliary body to the Schwalbe’s line.
  • The aqueous outflow system includes the trabecular meshwork, Schlemm’s canal, collector channels, aqueous veins, and the episcleral veins.
  • The uveal meshwork is the innermost part of the trabecular meshwork and extends from the iris root and ciliary body to the Schwalbe’s line.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition, Page No. 219-220

questions.stem: The mean values for outflow facility and uveoscleral outflow (percentage of total aqueous outflow facility) in normal eyes, respectively, are:
questions.solutionHtml:
0.28 μL/min/mmHg, 10% to 50%.
  • Outflow facility in normal eyes ranges from 0.22 to 0.28 μL/min/mmHg and decreases with age, ocular surgery, and trauma.
  • Patients with glaucoma often have decreased outflow facility.
  • Estimates of the value of uveoscleral outflow as a percentage of total aqueous outflow facilities may actually vary, with some being as low as 10%, and some as high as 50%.
  • Uveoscleral outflow is pressure-independent.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition, Page No. 219-224

questions.stem: The composition of aqueous solution is similar to that of plasma with a few exceptions. Compared with plasma, aqueous humour has an increased concentration of which one of these components?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ascorbate
  • Compared with plasma, aqueous solutions are slightly hypertonic and acidic.
  • Aqueous has a marked excess of ascorbate (15 times greater than that of arterial plasma) and a marked deficit of protein (0.2% in aqueous as compared to 7% in plasma)


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition, Page No. 221

questions.stem: Which of the nerve has the longest intracranial course?
questions.solutionHtml:
6th nerve
  • Abducens nerve has the longest intracranial course of all cranial nerves. It begins at its nucleus in the dorsal pons and courses superiorly and then anteriorly before leaving the brainstem at the pontomedullary junction. Because it has the longest intracranial course, it is most vulnerable to palsies due to raised intracranial tension.



Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 29-31

questions.stem: Aqueous humour is a clear tissue fluid that circulates through the anterior cavity of the eye. Which of the following statements about this fluid are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is produced from plasma by the ciliary epithelium of the pars plana.

options.label: B
options.text: Secretion is subject to the influence of the parasympathetic nervous system.

options.label: C
options.text: Aqueous flows from the anterior chamber via the pupil into the anterior chamber.

options.label: D
options.text: The enzymatic action of carbonic anhydrase is critical to its secretion.

questions.answerText: The enzymatic action of carbonic anhydrase is critical to its secretion.
questions.solutionHtml:
The enzymatic action of carbonic anhydrase is critical to its secretion.
  • Enzymatic action is critical in the secretion and flow of aqueous humour; carbonic anhydrase is among those playing a key role.


Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page No. 346

questions.stemHtml: Routes of aqueous outflow are shown in the given image. Which of the following statements is correct about the given image?

options.label: A
options.text: 90% of the aqueous flows through B

options.label: C
options.text: Aqueous humor flows through A into the Schlemm canal

options.label: D
options.text: C receives the most aqueous humor drainage

questions.answerText: Aqueous humor flows through A into the Schlemm canal
questions.solutionHtml:
Aqueous humor flows through A into the Schlemm canal

The given image shows the different routes of aqueous outflow.
(A) Trabecular;
(B) Uveoscleral;
(C) Iris

  • Aqueous humour is produced from plasma by the ciliary epithelium of the ciliary body pars plicata, using a combination of active and passive secretion.
  • A high-protein filtrate passes out of fenestrated capillaries (ultrafiltration) into the stroma of the ciliary processes, from which active transport of solutes occurs across the dual-layered ciliary epithelium.
  • The osmotic gradient thereby established facilitates the passive flow of water into the posterior chamber.
  • Secretion is subject to the influence of the sympathetic nervous system, with opposing actions mediated by beta-2 receptors (increased secretion) and alpha-2 receptors (decreased secretion).
  • Enzymatic action is also critical; carbonic anhydrase is among those playing a key role.


Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page No. 346

questions.stem: Aqueous fluid flows through the trabeculae into a mesh-like canal and then into the episcleral veins. Which of the following statements are incorrect about this canal?

options.label: A
options.text: The inner wall is lined by irregular spindle shaped endothelial cells

options.label: B
options.text: The outer wall is lined by smooth flat cells

options.label: C
options.text: Septa commonly divide the lumen into 7–8 channels

options.label: D
options.text: The described outflow route into the canal is a bulk flow pressure-sensitive route

questions.answerText: Septa commonly divide the lumen into 7–8 channels
questions.solutionHtml:
Septa commonly divide the lumen into 7–8 channels
  • The description given in the above question is of Schlemm’s Canal.
  • 90% of the aqueous flows through the trabeculae into the Schlemm canal and then the episcleral veins.
  • The Schlemm canal is a circumferential channel within the perilimbal sclera.
  • Septa commonly divide the lumen into 2–4 channels.


Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page No. 346

questions.stemHtml: Identify the structures depicted in the given Image from the normal anatomy of the outflow channels of aqueous humour and correctly label them to the given options. Select the correct answer from the given below ciode:
questions.solutionHtml:
1-c, 2-e, 3-b, 4-f
  • The normal anatomy of outflow channels for aqueous humour is shown in the given image.
  • Aqueous fluid flows from the posterior chamber via the pupil into the AC, from where it exits the eye via three routes.
  • Trabecular outflow (90%): aqueous fluid flows through the trabeculum into the Schlemm canal and then the episcleral veins.
  • This is a bulk flow pressure-sensitive route, so that increasing IOP will increase outflow.
  • Uveoscleral drainage (10%): aqueous fluid passes across the face of the ciliary body into the suprachoroidal space and is drained by the venous circulation in the ciliary body, choroid, and sclera.
  • Iris: Some aqueous fluid also drain via the iris. But this amount is physiologically insignificant.


Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page No. 346

questions.stem: Intraocular pressure (IOP) is determined by the balance between the rate of aqueous production and the rate of aqueous outflow. Which of the following statements is incorrect about intraocular pressure?

options.label: A
options.text: The upper range of normal for adults is 21 mmHg

options.label: B
options.text: The supine position leads to an increase in intraocular pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: The extent of glaucomatous damage is directly proportional to the likelihood of progressive visual field damage.

options.label: D
options.text: From a clinical point of view, the rate of aqueous formation is the most important factor.

questions.answerText: From a clinical point of view, the rate of aqueous formation is the most important factor.
questions.solutionHtml:
From a clinical point of view, the rate of aqueous formation is the most important factor.
  • The intraocular pressure (IOP) refers to the pressure exerted by intraocular fluids on the coats of the eyeball.
  • From a clinical point of view, resistance to aqueous outflow (drainage) is the most important factor.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 266, Comprehensive Ophthalmology by, A. K. Khurana’s , 7th Edition, Page Number: 223, Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page Number: 346, 347

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is the true statement regarding the corneal endothelium?

options.label: A
options.text: It consists of multiple layers of polygonal epithelial cells

options.label: B
options.text: The cell density of endothelium is around 5000 cells/mm2 in young adults

options.label: C
options.text: The loss of cells with age is compensated with multiplication of cells

options.label: D
options.text: The endothelial cells contain active pump mechanism which keeps cornea dehydrated

questions.answerText: The endothelial cells contain active pump mechanism which keeps cornea dehydrated
questions.solutionHtml:
The endothelial cells contain active pump mechanism which keeps cornea dehydrated
  • The active pump mechanism in endothelial cells keeps the cornea dehydrated and thus transparent.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition, Page No. 99

questions.stem: Which of the following is the long-term corneal preservation method?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryopreservation method
  • Cryopreservation of the corneal button at -70 degree can be done for up to 1 year.
  • Other long term methods include glycerine preservation and the organ culture method.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition, Page No. 142

questions.stem: Which of the following is beneficial for the patient? Suffering from gyrate atrophy of the choroid due to a deficiency of the enzyme ornithine transcarbomylase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arginine free diet
  • Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and the retina is a rare autosomal recessive retinal dystrophy characterized by progressive chorioretinal degeneration, early cataract formation, and myopia.
  • It is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme ornithine aminotransferase (OAT), which results in a 10- to 20-fold increase in plasma ornithine concentrations.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 336

Ring of Schwalbe
  • The cornea is composed of 5 discrete anatomical components, each with specific functions to achieve the goal of clarity and refractive potential.
  • The outermost component, the epithelium, provides a smooth surface due to the interactions of cytoskeletal components and the tear film matrix.
  • It also serves an important protective barrier function. The Bowman layer or membrane, the second layer, moving in towards the eye, serves as the smooth adhesion layer for the basement membrane of the epithelial cells.
  • This layer is not crucial for clarity or visual function since removal of the Bowman layer during photorefractive keratectomy does not negatively affect vision.
  • Termination of descemet membrane is Schwalbe's line.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 199

questions.stemHtml: Identify the ocular sign as shown in the Image
questions.solutionHtml:
Buphthalmos
  • In this condition, IOP is raised and the eyeball is enlarged as a whole. The enlarged cornea is usually associated with central or peripheral clouding and Descemet's tears (Haab's striae).


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 294

questions.stem: A 30-year-old patient has presented to you with a corneal epithelial defect. Which of the following modalities are ideal treatment strategies?Gundersen flapAmniotic membrane patch graftingCyanoacrylate glueLimbal stem cell transplantationSmoking cessationSelect the correct answer from the given below code:

options.label: B
options.text: a, b, c, d and e

questions.answerText: a, b, c, d and e
questions.solutionHtml:
a, b, c, d and e
  • A conjunctival (Gundersen) flap will protect and allow healing of a corneal epithelial defect.
    • It is particularly suitable for chronic unilateral disease, in which the prognosis for restoration of useful vision is poor.
    • The buccal mucous membrane is an alternative.
  • Amniotic membrane patch grafting can be used for persistent, unresponsive epithelial defects.
  • Tissue adhesive like cyanoacrylate glue is used to seal small perforations.
    • The glue can be applied to one side of a bespoke, trimmed patch of sterile plastic drape, which is pressed over the defect after the edges are dried with a cellulose sponge.
    • The patch remains in place to seal the defect, and a bandage contact lens is inserted for comfort and to aid retention of the patch.
  • Limbal stem cell transplantation may be used if there is a stem cell deficiency, as in chemical burns and cicatrizing conjunctivitis.
    • The source of the donor tissue may be the fellow eye (autograft) in unilateral disease or a living or cadaver donor (allograft) when both eyes are affected.
    • A newer technique involves the in vitro replication of the patient's own stem cells with subsequent reimplantation of the enhanced cell population.
  • Smoking retards epithelialization and should be discontinued.


Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach, 9th Edition, Page No. 209
